title: Stage inverse-image sheaf colimit on the affine site
statement: Let $I$ be a nonempty directed preorder and $D:I^{op}\to\mathrm{Scheme}$ a system of qcqs schemes with affine transition maps. Let $c$ be a limit cone and fix $i_0$ and a sheaf of sets $G$ on $D(i_0)$ [def-weil-pbc-sets-section-comparison]. On the full affine étale site [def-weil-pbc-full-affine-etale-site] of $D(i_0)$, set $A_j=(f_j)_*f_j^{-1}G$ and $L=p_*p^{-1}G$, restricted to that site, where $f_j=D(j\to i_0)$ and $p=c.\pi_{i_0}$. Any diagram $E$ and cocone $K$ with objects $A_j$, point $L$, and maps and legs equal componentwise to the canonical section comparisons is a colimit cocone in sheaves of sets. This assertion is at sheaf level and does not assert that evaluation preserves the colimit.

source.place: Tag 09YQ, proof via Sites Tags 09YN and 0A35

proof.text: Apply the affine-site colimit presentation to the cofinal upper tail. Use the inverse-image description of 0A35, local section representatives and local equality, then transport along full-affine restriction and unit-compatible composition. This identifies the sheafification of the stage presheaf colimit with the limit push-pull sheaf. The universal property of sheafification gives the colimit. The supplied component equations identify the diagram and cocone with these canonical maps. This step asserts local representatives, not preservation by evaluation.
